title: A Dataset You Can Trust: Demonstrations as Samples, a Scale Taken from the Training Part, and a Split by Episode

questions.question: A learner is tested on every fifth sample of its demonstrations and trained on the rest. Why might its test error be too good?
options: Every test sample has a training sample of its own episode a moment away, so memory alone scores well
Every fifth sample is always easier than the others
The test set is too large to be fair
The learner sees the test labels during training
questions.explanation: Neighbouring samples of an episode are 0.05 s apart and nearly identical. A learner that only remembers looks good on them, and will not on a new episode.

questions.question: A nearest neighbour was tested both ways on the same 4000 samples. What were its errors?
options: 0.00317 split by sample and 0.00118 split by episode
0.00118 split by sample and 0.00317 split by episode
The same both ways, 0.00118
0.00118 both ways, since the data was the same
questions.explanation: Split by episode the error was 2.7 times as large. The split by sample measured memory.

questions.question: How many episodes had samples in both the training and the test part, with each split?
options: 0 by sample and 40 by episode
Half of them either way
40 by sample and 0 by episode
None either way, since a sample is in one part only
questions.explanation: A sample is in one part, but its episode can be in both. Split by episode, none is.

questions.question: Where should the mean and spread used to scale the inputs come from?
options: From all the data, so the scale is as accurate as possible
From the test part, since that is what is measured
From the expert's gains
From the training part only
questions.explanation: The scale is part of the learned policy. Fitting it on the test part leaks the test into the training, a little, in the learner's favour.

questions.question: A policy will be used by a robot on days it has not seen. What should the test set be made of?
options: Whole days that were not in the training set
A random tenth of all the samples
The samples with the largest errors
The last sample of each day
questions.explanation: Split by the unit that is independent and that the policy will meet new: the episode, the day, the robot or the operator.

questions.question: An input never changed in the training data, so its spread is zero. What should the normaliser do?
options: Divide anyway, the result will be infinite and that is correct
Leave the input out and say so
Use a tiny spread so nothing is divided by zero, as fit_normaliser does
Use the spread of the other input
questions.explanation: Dividing by zero gives infinity or NaN, which then reaches the learner. A tiny spread keeps it finite; better still is to notice that the input carries no information.
